void.string: <GuidelineTitle> Measuring Blood Pressure at Clinic Visits
<MainFocus> This guideline sets out how blood pressure should be measured in adult primary care clinics so that readings are comparable between visits and between clinicians.
<RecommendationStrengthRatingScheme> graded each recommendation as strong or conditional
<InclusionCriterion> Adults aged 18 years or older attending a routine clinic visit.
<Recommendation> Measure blood pressure after the patient has been seated quietly for at least five minutes.
<Directive> Measure blood pressure after the patient has been seated quietly for at least five minutes
<Recommendation> Use a validated automated device with a cuff sized to the upper arm of the patient.
<Directive> Use a validated automated device with a cuff sized to the upper arm of the patient
<Recommendation> If the first reading is 140/90 mm Hg or higher, take two further readings one minute apart and record the average of the last two.
<DecisionVariable> the first reading is 140/90 mm Hg or higher
<Action> take two further readings one minute apart and record the average of the last two
<Logic> If the first reading is 140/90 mm Hg or higher is [true] Then take two further readings one minute apart and record the average of the last two
<ScheduledReview> This guideline will be reviewed every three years, or sooner if new evidence appears.
